result.markdown: --- title: "Bayesian inference" course-unit: ch09-bayesian-inference status: complete --- ## Why this unit matters - Chapter 8: parameters are fixed unknowns, uncertainty is sampling variability. - **Bayesian view:** parameters are random variables; a **prior** is updated into a **posterior** by the data. - Same SIR model, same reports — different treatment of uncertainty, with [Turing.jl](https://turinglang.org/). ::: {.notes} The engine changes from optimisation to MCMC sampling, and the output changes from a point estimate plus interval to a full posterior distribution. ::: ## Bayes' theorem for the SIR model $$ p(\theta\mid y_{1:n})=\frac{p(y_{1:n}\mid\theta)\,p(\theta)}{p(y_{1:n})}, $$ same Poisson likelihood as Chapter 8, with weakly informative priors on the natural $[0,1]$ ranges: $$ i_0\sim\operatorname{Beta}(1,20),\qquad \beta\sim\operatorname{Beta}(1,10). $$ The normalising constant is intractable; **NUTS** draws samples whose histogram approximates the posterior. ::: {.notes} Prior means $1/21\approx0.048$ and $1/11\approx0.091$ are broad near the truth ($i_0=0.01,\beta=0.05$) but supported only on plausible values. ::: ## The probabilistic model and sampler ::: {#cell-ch09-diagnostics .cell execution_count=1} ::: {#ch09-diagnostics .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (max_rhat = 1.018, posterior_mean = (i₀ = 0.009, β = 0.0501), truth = (i₀ = 0.01, β = 0.05)) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.notes} Three hundred draws over two chains run fast enough to demonstrate live while still giving a meaningful $\hat R$. Say out loud that a real analysis wants more. NUTS differentiates through the ODE solve via `SciMLSensitivity`. ::: ## Posterior and predictive check ::: {#cell-fig-slide-ch09-posterior .cell execution_count=1} ::: {#fig-slide-ch09-posterior .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` Left: marginal posteriors (blue) around the truth (red). Right: 95% posterior predictive band vs the data (grey). ::: ::: ::: {.notes} The predictive band envelops the data; the marginals concentrate around the truth. The book chapter also shows trace plots and full $\hat R$ / ESS tables. ::: ## Takeaways and limitations - `@model` + `NUTS` turns Bayes' theorem into executable sampling. - Check convergence with $\hat R\approx1$ and effective sample size. - Priors are modelling choices; guard the ODE solve and floor the rate. - NUTS re-solves + differentiates the ODE each step — costlier than Chapter 8. - $\beta$–$c$ non-identifiability persists; Poisson still assumes equidispersion. Read the [book chapter](../../chapters/09-bayesian-inference.html); see [Turing.jl](https://turinglang.org/) and [MCMCChains.jl](https://turinglang.org/MCMCChains.jl/stable/). ::: {.notes} The central advantage: Bayesian inference makes assumptions explicit and propagates them directly into the posterior predictive distribution. :::
